chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Writing for King Records: Henry Glover and Dossie Terry
summary: With Charlie Singleton and Glover, McRae wrote songs for Wynonie Harris and the "Thunderbird" jingle.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But I (inaudible) Charlie Singleton, we did -- one time we did a lot of things. We did like "Ding Dong Buggy, Person To Person Blues." Thing called "All Night Long." You got a list of them there.
And we did a lot of things for King at that time.
King Records.
King Records.
At that time, I was writing for King with Glover. I did a lot of things personally for Glover like "All She Wanna Do Is Rock with Wynonie Harris," back in those days, you know.
You know, it was a lot of rock and roll

Una Mae, she's figured not very well known about. Does she ever talk about her family and so forth?
She was very -- no. Una Mae Carlisle?

She was a very talented girl. If you met her once, you know, you'll always remember her, because that's the type of person -- she was a delightful artist would grow on you. I guess that's why people call her Fats Waller, because she was really ahead her time, I think.

She had great ideas about writing. I can't remember some of the other things she did, but she was really well known, you know. One of the outstanding writers I had a chance to meet, you know, when I was coming up.
I think that she was from an Indian family out there in Ohio.
Yeah.
DownBeat, I think, did a couple of articles on her. Ebony also did an article on her before she died.
It's a shame she died rather young.
Yeah.
You know, travelling so much, sometime you be with people and the next time you come in town, they passed away.
I never did know what she died up or anything. I know that -- (inaudible) with Cab at that time or some band. I know I was travelling a lot.

I guess it was breast cancer or something like that.
Yeah. Well we had did --
